flags.item: Next Gen Stats Week 2 passing table
flags.detail: The official page rendered only the NGS logo shell on 4 attempts; Week 2 QB rows are left blank and excluded from prop work.
nfl.com labels the game 'Sunday Night Football, September 9th', but 2026-09-09 is a Wednesday. Recorded verbatim.

Schedule renders label kickoff times 'LOCAL' without naming a time zone (Weeks 9 and 10); times are shown exactly as rendered. Root data/schedule-2026-week9.json labels the same times ET — not confirmed by the page itself.

The standings legend does not name columns 14 and 16. Their values equal each team's non-conference record and last-5 record for 32/32 teams (512/512 cells in results/standings-reconciliation-2026-11-14.json); the labels are inferred, the values are official.
Some team-weeks have no NGS row (e.g. TB Week 7; JAX and TB Week 8). These team-games are excluded, never filled.
Each line assumes the team's most recent NGS passer (Weeks 1, 3–8) starts. Starters are not confirmed by an official source here; check the official injury report before use.

flags.item: Week 10 lines ignore injuries and QB changes
flags.detail: Ratings use final scores only. Example: per NGS, BAL's Week 8 passer was Joe Fagnano; a score-only model cannot price such changes.

4 of 12 strategies passed all eight gates on the extended W3–W9 window (original W3–W8 run: 0 of 12; the Week 9 slate drove the change). Passing = statistically detectable skill vs pre-registered naive baselines on official scores — NOT profit: no market prices exist, so ROI/EV is never computed. Best: S6 (win probability), skill +5.43%, Holm p = 0.0012.
No official source publishes sportsbook prices, so any 'edge vs book' strategy fails G8 here. The root dashboard's candidates rely on data/market-lines.json (flagged unverified by earlier sessions).

First render of the Week 2 scores page showed 9 games as 'Hidden Score'; one Week 6 render was an empty skeleton. Re-fetching the same official URLs showed all values; every score is confirmed by the 512/512 standings reconciliation.

Multiple sessions claim root integration; PRs #36–#38 merged while this session's board claim was unpushed to main, producing two independent Week 10 origins (see OF-18). This session rebased onto main and force-updated only its own branch once after the initial push was rejected.

nfl.com renders the Rams as LA in some views and LAR in others (Week 9: scores page LAR, schedule page LA — same games, same scores). Root data and this lab use LAR; the cross-check maps LA↔LAR. Same team; values agree.

flags.item: Next Gen Stats Week 9 passing table
flags.detail: https://nextgenstats.nfl.com/stats/passing/2026/REG/9 rendered empty (logo shell only) on 4 attempts on 2026-11-14, while Week 8 renders normally. Week 9 QB props are therefore not evaluable; the prop evaluation window stays Weeks 4–8. No values were filled.

WAS 24, NYG 21 (Thursday, November 12th) was final before origination. It is excluded from the 13 Week 10 lines to avoid grading a known result, recorded under w10-lines.json → excluded_completed, and its result is on the Week 10 scores page.

The official injuries capture at URL .../injuries/league/2026/reg9 renders the page title '2026 Injuries' (league year) while the path says reg9 (2025). The 2026 injuries page was used only for manual starter checks, never as a data input.

nfl.com returns 404 for /depth-charts/ and /teams/<team>/depth-chart/ (checked 2026-11-14). Roster pages exist but list no depth ordering. String-level depth (2nd/3rd-string replacements) therefore cannot be confirmed officially and is left blank — never inferred.

results/w9-lines.json renders fair_spread_text from the favourite's perspective while the numeric field is the home margin — a labelling hazard flagged by session f6e60a81. That frozen file is never edited; the Week 10 output carries explicit fields (fair_spread_favourite_text, fair_spread_favourite_team, fair_handicap_home_pts, fair_home_margin_S1) so the perspectives cannot be confused.

This session's board claim (2026-11-14 01:03 UTC) and session f6e60a81's PR #38 (merged 01:08 UTC) both originated Week 10 lines without seeing each other's section. Both are published: theirs in requirements/results/week10-lines.json (B0 rate benchmark + Elo), this lab's in results/w10-lines.json (walk-forward ridge). Cross-check: favourite side agrees 13/13; mean home-margin difference 0.2 points.

flags.detail: Week 9 final scores page renders the Rams as LAR; the Week 9 schedule page renders LA. Values identical (NYG 19–11 PHI; LAR 20–13 WAS). Recorded in results/w9-checks.json; abbreviations mapped in the cross-check.
